jobs.title: Investment Banking Analyst - Municipals
jobs.description:
Investment Banking Analyst - Municipal Finance

Location: Dallas, TX

Business Unit: Municipal Finance Investment Banking

Position Summary

Jefferies is seeking a highly motivated Investment Banking Analyst to join its Municipal Finance team in Dallas. The Analyst will work closely with senior bankers in providing strategic advisory and capital markets solutions to municipal issuers, governmental entities, nonprofit organizations, higher education institutions, healthcare systems, transportation agencies, and other public sector clients.

The Analyst will play an integral role in transaction execution, financial analysis, debt structuring, client presentations, and business development initiatives. This position offers significant exposure to senior professionals, clients, and complex financing transactions across the municipal capital markets landscape.

Primary Responsibilities

- Conduct detailed financial analysis and quantitative modeling related to municipal bond financings and capital market transactions.

- Assist in the execution of tax-exempt and taxable bond offerings, refundings, and other public finance transactions.

- Prepare financing scenarios, debt affordability analyses, and capital planning models.

- Develop pitch books, client presentations, requests for proposal (RFP) responses, and marketing materials.

- Analyze municipal issuer financial statements, budgets, economic data, and credit profiles.

- Support due diligence efforts and coordinate transaction processes with clients, bond counsel, rating agencies, underwriters, and other stakeholders.

- Monitor municipal market conditions, interest rate trends, and regulatory developments.

- Conduct industry and sector research on education, healthcare, transportation, utilities, housing, and local government issuers.

- Maintain transaction databases and support business development opportunities across Texas and the broader Southwest region.

- Participate in client meetings, financing discussions, and strategic planning engagements.

Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, Public Policy, Mathematics, or a related field.

- Strong academic record with demonstrated analytical ability.

- 1 to 2 years of experience in investment banking, public finance, municipal advisory, accounting, consulting, or capital markets preferred.

- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint.

- Strong quantitative, financial modeling, and presentation skills.

- Excellent written and verbal communication abilities.

- Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.

- Ability to manage multiple projects and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

- Demonstrated interest in municipal finance and public sector capital markets.

Preferred Qualifications

- Coursework or experience related to public finance, fixed income markets, economics, or governmental accounting.

- Exposure to municipal bond financing structures and credit analysis.

- Familiarity with Bloomberg, Capital IQ, DBC Finance, MuniOS, or similar financial platforms.

- Progress toward CFA, Series 52, Series 63, or other relevant securities licenses is a plus.

Salary Range of $110,000-$125,000

jobs.title: Investment Banking Analyst – Strategic Finance and Shareholder Engagement & Activism Advisory
jobs.description:
Shareholder Engagement & Activism Advisory (SEAA) and Strategic Finance Group (SFG)

About the Groups:

Shareholder Engagement & Activism Advisory (SEAA):

SEAA advises public companies, Boards of Directors, and senior executives on activism preparedness and response strategies, shareholder engagement, governance matters, and complicated M&A situations. The team provides strategic insights and analysis needed to support the critical advice it provides to clients as they navigate complex shareholder dynamics and seek to drive long-term value creation.

Strategic Finance Group (SFG)

SFG partners with Boards of Directors, and senior executive teams on high-impact strategic decisions, including valuation analysis, strategic alternatives reviews, portfolio optimization, corporate transformations, capital deployment, M&A capital markets, and capital structure design. Known for its analytical rigor and proprietary frameworks, SFG helps clients unlock sustainable shareholder value.

The Role

Jefferies is seeking a driven and intellectually curious Analyst to join our growing M&A Advisory platform in New York, supporting both the Shareholder Engagement & Activism Advisory and Strategic Finance Groups. The scope of work will be multi-disciplinary, extending across M&A, capital markets and legal areas of expertise, and well as typical investment banking core competencies such as financial modeling and data analysis. This role offers a rare opportunity to work directly with senior leaders and subject matter experts on high-impact, board-level strategic and financial advisory engagements.

As an Analyst, you will collaborate across industry coverage and product teams to deliver strategic advice to corporate clients. You will play a key role in developing shareholder defense materials, building complex financial models, and creating intellectual capital that supports governance, M&A, and corporate finance engagements.

Key Responsibilities

- Support SEAA and SFG teams in live engagements and business development initiatives

- Build and maintain complex financial models and valuation analyses

- Perform shareholder register assessments and analysis of investor portfolios

- Evaluation of activist shareholder past performance and provide insights into potential tactics and strategies

- Develop shareholder engagement and activism defense materials

- Conduct strategic alternatives reviews and capital structure assessments

- Analyze corporate governance frameworks, bylaws, board structures, and takeover defenses

- Contribute to proprietary tools, databases, and knowledge assets

- Collaborate with senior bankers and cross-functional teams in a fast-paced environment

- Prepare client presentations and participate in internal and external meetings

Skills & Attributes

- Strong foundation in M&A, capital markets, valuation, and corporate strategy

- Advanced proficiency in Excel (including data analysis) and PowerPoint; strong financial modeling skills required

- Experience with financial databases (e.g., DealPointData, Bloomberg, Capital IQ, Refinitiv, FactSet, Diligent, ISS)

- Ability to interpret financial statements, investor presentations, and governance documents

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills; confident presenting to senior stakeholders

- Collaborative mindset with the ability to thrive in team-based environments

- Creative problem-solving skills and comfort with ambiguity

- High attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities

Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, Mathematics, or related field with strong academic performance

- Must have one plus year of investment banking experience

- Prior internship or work experience in investment banking, consulting, law, or corporate finance preferred

- Demonstrated interest in corporate finance, shareholder activism, governance, and M&A advisory

The salary range for this role is $110,00- $125,000

jobs.title: SVP, Head of Enterprise AI Program Management
jobs.description:
The Head of Enterprise AI Program Management will provide the program management discipline required to turn Jefferies’ Enterprise AI strategy into an executable, measurable firmwide delivery program. The role will coordinate and govern delivery across the AI workstreams, ensuring scope, ownership, milestones, dependencies, risks, and outcomes are clearly defined and actively managed.

This position requires strong project and program management capability, executive presence, financial and commercial judgment, and the ability to create structure, momentum, and accountability across a complex, matrixed AI transformation program.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise AI Program Management

- Establish and operate the Enterprise AI PMO, including program governance, reporting cadence, delivery standards, dependency tracking, escalation paths, and decision forums.

- Translate the multi-year AI strategy into an integrated program plan with workstreams, accountable owners, milestones, dependencies, required inputs, and measurable outcomes.

- Maintain a single enterprise view of roadmap progress, risks, issues, actions, decisions, dependencies, resource constraints, and executive follow-ups across the AI program.

Use Case Intake, Planning & Prioritization

- Manage the AI use-case intake process and ensure proposals are captured consistently with business objective, sponsor, expected value, feasibility, delivery approach, control considerations, and required funding.

- Coordinate prioritization discussions so leadership can evaluate use cases against strategic value, readiness, complexity, cost, delivery capacity, risk, and expected adoption.

- Partner with business transformation leads and workstream owners to convert approved use cases into clear project plans, milestones, acceptance criteria, and success metrics.

Funding Governance, ROI & Value Realization

- Support milestone-based funding governance across approval, proof-of-value, scale-up, and transition to business-as-usual, in partnership with Finance and accountable initiative owners.

- Partner with the CFO organization and Controllers to validate assumptions, baselines, savings, realized outcomes, and ongoing investment performance.

- Produce portfolio-level views of investment, forecast, value at risk, realized benefits, adoption, and expected returns for senior leadership.

Delivery Coordination & RAID Management

- Coordinate delivery across cross-functional AI workstreams and pods by aligning accountable technical, business, and control-function owners around shared plans, milestones, and outcomes.

- Maintain integrated project plans, timelines, milestone trackers, RAID logs, dependency maps, action registers, and escalation items across the Enterprise AI Program.

- Facilitate structured delivery cadences, identify blockers early, drive follow-ups to resolution, and help ensure workstream owners have the inputs and decisions needed to maintain execution momentum.

Financial Management, FinOps & Cost Transparency

- Track program-level budget, forecast, resource assumptions, funding approvals, and financial reporting inputs for the Enterprise AI Program in partnership with Technology Finance and workstream owners.

- Partner with FinOps and Technology Finance to establish transparency over compute, token consumption, infrastructure, licenses, vendor, and consulting costs.

- Provide clear views of committed spend, utilization, run rate, forecast variance, cost risks, and linkage to approved use cases and business outcomes.

Controls, Risk & Regulatory Readiness

- Coordinate with security, data governance, privacy, legal, compliance, model risk, architecture, and audit partners to embed required controls into the program lifecycle.

- Help ensure initiatives progress through defined control gates with appropriate documentation, approvals, evidence, and traceability.

- Maintain program-level risk reporting and support timely escalation of material control issues, decisions, and remediation actions through the appropriate forums.

Executive Reporting & Stakeholder Management

- Prepare concise, decision-oriented status reporting for the CIO, CFO, Enterprise AI leadership, steering forums, QBRs, and other senior governance venues.

- Facilitate working sessions and leadership forums, capture decisions, document actions, confirm owners, track deadlines, and support timely escalation where needed.

- Act as a central coordination point for program status, priorities, risks, dependencies, escalations, and accountability across business, technology, and corporate functions.

Change, Adoption & Organizational Readiness

- Partner with Change and Training leadership to embed communications, role-based enablement, safe-use guidance, feedback loops, and adoption measures into funded initiatives.

- Support divisional champion models and strengthen local ownership of outcomes, utilization, workflow change, and sustained business impact.

- Coordinate launch- and scale-readiness reviews to ensure capabilities can be adopted safely and sustainably.

Qualifications & Experience

- Significant experience supporting or managing large-scale technology, AI, digital transformation, or strategic programs within financial services or another complex, regulated environment.

- Proven ability to bring structure to complex or evolving programs through integrated project plans, governance routines, RAID management, stakeholder forums, milestone tracking, and executive reporting.

- Strong understanding of program delivery, portfolio management, business-case development, prioritization, financial governance, benefits realization, risk management, and organizational change.

- Demonstrated ability to influence senior business, technology, finance, and control-function leaders without relying on direct authority.

- Exceptional written, verbal, financial, commercial, and executive communication skills, including the ability to create concise decision-ready materials.

Preferred Experience

- Experience managing AI, automation, digital transformation, data, platform, infrastructure, or innovation delivery programs within investment banking, capital markets, or broader financial services.

- Familiarity with enterprise AI operating models, responsible AI, model and data controls, FinOps, consumption-based technology economics, and regulated technology environments.

- Working familiarity with AI delivery concepts such as use-case lifecycle management, model/data dependencies, production readiness, responsible AI controls, evaluation, adoption tracking, and post-implementation monitoring.

- Experience with scaled product delivery, cross-functional pods, use-case lifecycle governance, and transition from pilot to production.

Primary Location Full Time Salary Range of $225,000 - $300,000.

jobs.title: VP, AI Strategy & Execution Lead
jobs.description:
The AI Specialist will partner closely with Risk subject matter experts, Technology teams, and firmwide AI governance stakeholders to help define, develop, and execute the Risk department’s AI strategy. This role will support the buildout of the Risk AI roadmap, operating model, and implementation plan, with a focus on identifying high-value AI opportunities, translating business needs into scalable AI solutions, and ensuring responsible AI adoption across the Risk function.

The ideal candidate will bring strong AI expertise, an understanding of risk management processes, and the ability to work across business, technology, governance, and senior management stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities
AI Strategy and Roadmap Support

- Support the development and execution of the Risk department’s AI strategy, roadmap, operating model, and implementation plan.

- Partner with Risk leadership and subject matter experts to identify AI opportunities across risk management processes.

- Help evaluate, prioritize, and assess the feasibility, value, and adoption potential of AI use cases within Risk.

- Contribute to the articulation of Risk’s AI strategy, progress, opportunities, and risks for senior management audiences.

AI Use Case Development and Execution

- Work with Risk SMEs to define and execute prioritized AI use cases.

- Translate business requirements into scalable, practical AI solutions.

- Advise on appropriate AI models, tools, technologies, and solution approaches based on business needs, data availability, control requirements, and enterprise standards.

- Support the full AI use case lifecycle, including ideation, requirements gathering, solution design, testing, deployment, enhancement, and ongoing monitoring.

- Partnership with Technology Teams

- Collaborate closely with relevant Technology teams to support AI solution development, integration, testing, and enterprise deployment.

- Help ensure AI solutions are scalable, maintainable, secure, and aligned with enterprise technology architecture and standards.

- Serve as a bridge between Risk stakeholders and Technology teams to ensure clear communication of requirements, constraints, priorities, and delivery timelines.

AI Adoption, Training, and Change Management

- Promote AI adoption across the Risk department by educating stakeholders on AI capabilities, limitations, and relevant use cases.

- Monitor and communicate developments in AI technology, industry trends, and emerging best practices relevant to risk management.

- Facilitate AI training, education sessions, and knowledge-sharing forums for Risk users.

- Support change management efforts to embed AI tools and processes into day-to-day Risk workflows.

AI Governance, Controls, and Risk Management

- Work with firmwide AI governance teams to ensure appropriate control processes are established for Risk AI usage.

- Support governance processes related to AI use case approval, data controls, model or code review, guardrails, testing, documentation, access management, change management, and ongoing monitoring.

- Ensure AI solutions are implemented in accordance with applicable internal policies, risk standards, and regulatory expectations.

- Help identify, document, and escalate potential risks related to AI adoption, including data quality, privacy, model performance, bias, operational risk, and control gaps.

Required Qualifications

- Experience working with AI, machine learning, generative AI, data science, analytics, or related technologies.

- Strong understanding of AI solution design, model evaluation, data requirements, testing, deployment, and ongoing monitoring.

- Experience translating business requirements into technology-enabled solutions.

- Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to partner effectively across business, technology, governance, and control functions.

- Excellent communication skills, including the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences and present effectively to senior stakeholders.

- Strong analytical, problem-solving, and project execution skills.

- Ability to operate in a highly controlled, regulated, and fast-paced environment.

Primary Location Full Time Salary Range of $225,000 - $250,000.

jobs.title: VP, Program Manager - Global Information Security
jobs.description:
The VP of Information Security Program Management is a senior delivery leader responsible for the health, governance, and execution of the Information Security program portfolio. This is not a traditional project coordination role — we are looking for a highly assertive program executive with strong presence who can operate effectively in a complex, fast-moving environment. The right candidate drives execution, challenges weak plans, surfaces uncomfortable truths early, and ensures risks and issues are addressed before they impact delivery.

The role sits within the Cybersecurity COO organization and carries dual accountability: owning the day-to-day delivery of the Information Security portfolio while simultaneously building and maturing the program management operating model that the function runs on. This leader will inherit a function in active transformation — navigating an organizational redesign, a Global Capability Center build, a vendor optimization program, and the stand-up of Data Security and AI Security capabilities.

Responsibilities

- Own the integrated Information Security delivery portfolio, maintaining a unified, real-time view of all programs and projects including status, milestones, dependencies, risks, decisions, and resource utilization.

- Build and maintain standardized dashboards, scorecards, and executive reporting that are readily accessible to leadership and key stakeholders.

- Track and monitor portfolio health; ensure risks and issues are escalated with sufficient lead time for leadership action.

- Own the CISO portfolio reporting and escalations process — ensuring the right information reaches the right audience at the right cadence.

- Drive accountability across stakeholders; ensure actions, decisions, and commitments are tracked transparently and closed on time.

- Establish a communications plan for delivery reporting, defining report types, audiences, and cadences that support efficient delivery without unnecessary overhead.

- Coordinate security-related initiatives across the portfolio including identity and access management, SSO, PAM, segregation of duties, security operations, network security, physical security, application onboarding, and regulatory readiness.

- Define, implement, and continuously improve the Information Security program management operating model — establishing the frameworks, templates, tools, and governance routines the function operates on.

- Collaborate with IT organizations across the firm to identify and adopt best practices; ensure Information Security delivery standards are aligned with broader technology organization norms.

- Establish and lead recurring governance forums with the CISO leadership team where portfolio health, risks, and priorities are reviewed.

- Serve as a neutral point of alignment, ensuring objectivity and balance across delivery areas.

- Lead and develop a team of Project Managers and Business Analysts embedded across the Information Security portfolio with influence rather than authority.

- Set clear performance expectations; hold team members accountable to delivery quality, stakeholder engagement, and professional conduct.

- Model a 'trust but verify' mindset — coaching PMs to validate status through evidence and data rather than accepting optimistic self-reporting.

- Lead the annual Information Security investment planning cycle end-to-end, from demand intake and business case development through prioritization, budget submission, and approval.

- Maintain alignment between strategic priorities and funded initiatives throughout the year, surfacing gaps, over-allocations, and trade-off decisions to leadership in real time.

- Partner with Finance and the Cybersecurity COO to track actuals vs. plan; produce variance analysis and reforecast submissions as required.

- Own benefits realization tracking for all approved investments, ensuring outcomes committed to in business cases are measured, reported, and achieved.

- Partner closely with global technology teams to align Information Security delivery with firm-wide technology programs, shared platforms, and enterprise architecture decisions.

- Identify and manage cross-program dependencies between Information Security initiatives and broader technology portfolio commitments.

- Represent Information Security delivery in firm-wide program governance forums; ensure cybersecurity priorities are visible and protected within the broader investment landscape.

- Identify process inefficiencies and control gaps within delivery and governance; recommend and implement targeted improvements that enhance visibility, predictability, and execution speed.

- Facilitate lessons-learned reviews across programs and integrate findings into governance standards and delivery frameworks.

- Champion automation of portfolio management processes using available tooling, reducing manual reporting overhead and improving data quality and timeliness.

Qualifications

- 8+ years of program management experience within Information Security, Cybersecurity, Technology Risk, or Enterprise Technology.

- Demonstrated experience building or leading a PMO or portfolio governance function — not just managing individual programs.

- Experience leading large-scale transformation, integration, or organizational change programs in complex, matrixed environments.

- Strong working knowledge of vendor risk management, security governance, identity and access management, and technology risk.

- Proven experience leading and developing teams of Project Managers and Business Analysts — setting standards, building capability, and managing performance.

- Track record of leading annual investment planning cycles from demand intake through budget submission and approval.

- Experience partnering with senior technology and business leadership and navigating cross-functional dependencies at scale.

- Experience delivering in a global, distributed operating model including coordination with offshore or GCC-based teams.

- Financial services experience strongly preferred; familiarity with regulatory environments, governance standards, and audit readiness is essential.

- Familiarity with AI-assisted PM tooling, portfolio dashboards, and reporting automation preferred.

- PMP certification required or actively in progress; PRINCE2, SAFe, or Agile equivalent a plus.

- CISSP, CISM, or CRISC certification a plus.

Primary Location Full Time Salary Range of $185,000 - $200,000.

Investment Banking – Mergers & Acquisitions (Greek Speaker)

Analyst / Associate
